parts.name: the driving caution and the shortcut paragraph (batch 474, re-run)
parts.text:
There is something you should never do while using this induction. And that’s use it, practice it or test it while you’re driving or doing something where you need to be actively paying attention. It’s just not safe to be going into a trance where you are actively paying attention to what’s going on inside of you when you need to be paying attention to what’s going on outside of you. Even though your eyes can be open, even though you’re using “if it would be useful for you to do so” type language it’s just not safe.
If you want to turn this one off, simply don’t practice it anymore. Take it out of your recordings, take it out of your apps if you’re using it in an app, and start using your regular induction. Tell yourself, when you’re awake, that you won’t be using it anymore. Just because you say that it’ll be gone doesn’t mean that it’ll be gone right away. If it’s causing you a problem, if you’re still responding to it when you don’t want to respond to it, if you’re having issues with disorientation, etc, get some help from someone who’s qualified to help you with this. If, on the other hand, you want to keep it so that you can use it to go back into trance at a later date when you do want to go into a trance, that’s fine too. For now, though, once you come out of this trance, it’ll be over for today.

parts.name: the return's check paragraph (batch 474)
parts.text: When you come out, remind yourself what day (or date) it is. Look to your left and your right. Look at something near, and something far. Move around a bit. Don’t get up until you feel like you can do so without falling over. Make sure that you are oriented and alert (counting does this, but not always). Take mental note of only what actually came up for you and any actions you need to take regarding it. Then go on and do something normal.

parts.name: Nothing happens' two lines and It feels fake's question (batch 474)

Show yourself one body sensation, one word, ask yourself if you want to listen today or if you need to rest.
Do you have a sense of what it is that feels fake? The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc.

parts.name: the return paragraph (batch 473, unchanged since this morning)
parts.text: If you have done anything to alter your state when coming out of a trance, make sure to reverse those things. If you have floated, make sure to gain your weight again (whatever weight you want of course). If you have shrunk, make sure to grow back to your regular size. If you have met a younger state or are working with parts, make sure to come back to feeling complete in your body in the here and now, that your body belongs to you, and that it is under control of your adult mind. If you have gone somewhere, make sure to go back the same way you went there. Etcetera. Make sure to only take with you when you come out of a session the things that you want to!

parts.name: his forces paragraph (unchanged since this morning)
parts.text: One of the best side-effects of learning self-hypnosis is that sudden “waking up” to all the ways your attention is being shaped in your day-to-day life. There are actually multiple patents on using screens to send subliminal messages, but even without that kind of potentially illegal tech, the screen is one connection to the omnipotent Algorithm. Which shows us ads and guides our preferences. Then we wonder why we vote for this or that politician. But there are also the older, more mundane influences: erotic imprinting (as if breast implants are actually sexy), religious fear, which tags along with shame, charismatic authority and pressure to belong. And all of that drilled repeatedly into us, because one exposure won’t do the trick. Sometimes it’s benign – like lullabies or prayers or being taught by a good teacher or listening to a beautiful song or being in love. But you may want to ask yourself what effect it’s having on your ability to see clearly and make choices.
